# Flair CLI surface snapshot (flair#1619)
# Byte-identical gate for src/cli.ts modularization. Do not edit by hand.
# Refresh: UPDATE_CLI_SURFACE_SNAPSHOT=1 bun test test/unit-isolated/cli-surface-snapshot.test.ts
# helpWidth=80 (pinned; TTY columns must not affect this file)
# commands=129 options=549
#
# TREE is registration order: every command/subcommand + declared options/args.
# HELP is each command's outputHelp() (--help, including addHelpText).
# Homedir and the CLI version are replaced so a bump/$HOME change is not a miss.

flair
  usage: [options] [command]
  options:
    -v, --version
      description: output the version number
      attr: version
  subcommands: init, agent, keys, hook, mcp, principal, idp, grant, revoke, federation, rem, status, snapshot, upgrade, stop, start, restart, uninstall, reembed, test, deploy, fleet, doctor, quality, session, memory, search, bootstrap, relationship, soul, bridge, backup, restore, export, import, inspect, migrate-harness-memory, presence, workspace, orgevent, attention

flair init
  description: One-command Flair setup — bootstrap the instance, register an agent, and wire MCP clients
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --agent-id <id>
      description: Agent ID to register (omit to bootstrap instance without agent)
      attr: agentId
    --agent <id>
      description: Alias for --agent-id
      attr: agent
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port (default: this instance's current port, or 19926 for a new one)
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --ops-bind <addr>
      description: Harper ops API bind address (env: FLAIR_OPS_BIND; default: 127.0.0.1 loopback-only for single-host — pass e.g. 0.0.0.0 for multi-host/Fabric remote admin)
      attr: opsBind
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (generated if omitted)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-pass-file <path>
      description: Read admin password from file (chmod 600 recommended)
      attr: adminPassFile
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username when authenticating to an already-running instance via --target/--ops-target (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin — local bootstrap and Fabric provisioning always create 'admin')
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory for Ed25519 keys
      attr: keysDir
    --data-dir <dir>
      description: Harper data directory
      attr: dataDir
    --skip-start
      description: Skip Harper startup (assume already running)
      attr: skipStart
    --skip-soul
      description: Skip interactive personality setup
      attr: skipSoul
    --client <client>
      description: Client(s) to wire: claude-code, codex, gemini, cursor, antigravity, pi (native extension), all, or none
      attr: client
    --no-mcp
      description: Skip MCP client wiring (instance + agent only)
      attr: mcp
      negate: true
    --skip-smoke
      description: Skip the MCP smoke test
      attr: skipSmoke
    --skip-claude-md
      description: Skip appending the Flair bootstrap line to CLAUDE.md (claude-code only)
      attr: skipClaudeMd
    --skip-hook
      description: Skip installing the flair-session-start SessionStart hook (claude-code and Codex)
      attr: skipHook
    --target <url>
      description: Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
      attr: target
    --remote
      description: When used with --target, init as hub for remote federation
      attr: remote
    --ops-target <url>
      description: Explicit ops API URL (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET; bypasses port derivation)
      attr: opsTarget
    --force
      description: Skip confirmation prompt for remote writes (required with --target)
      attr: force
    --cluster-admin-user <user>
      description: Harper cluster admin username (env: FLAIR_CLUSTER_ADMIN_USER)
      attr: clusterAdminUser
    --cluster-admin-pass <pass>
      description: Harper cluster admin password (env: FLAIR_CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASS)
      attr: clusterAdminPass
    --flair-admin-pass <pass>
      description: Password for Flair's admin user (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS; generated if omitted)
      attr: flairAdminPass

flair agent
  description: Manage Flair agents
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: add, list, show, rotate-key, remove

flair agent add
  description: Register a new agent in a running Flair instance
  usage: [options] <id>
  arguments:
    id (required)
  options:
    --name <name>
      description: Display name (defaults to id)
      attr: name
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password for registration
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-pass-file <path>
      description: Read the admin password from a file (chmod 600 enforced). Preferred over inline --admin-pass — keeps the secret out of ps and shell history; works for remote targets too (an explicit flag is operator intent).
      attr: adminPassFile
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory for Ed25519 keys
      attr: keysDir
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --target <url>
      description: Remote Flair REST URL; derives the ops API URL (port-1) to seed the Agent there (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
      attr: target
    --ops-target <url>
      description: Explicit ops API URL to seed the Agent on (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET; bypasses port derivation)
      attr: opsTarget

flair agent list
  description: List all agents
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID to authenticate as via Ed25519 (or FLAIR_AGENT_ID env) when no admin pass
      attr: agent
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory holding the agent's Ed25519 key
      attr: keysDir
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --json
      description: Emit raw JSON array (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)
      attr: json

flair agent remove
  description: Remove an agent and all its data from Flair
  usage: [options] <id>
  arguments:
    id (required)
  options:
    --keep-keys
      description: Do not delete key files from disk
      attr: keepKeys
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory for Ed25519 keys
      attr: keysDir
    --force
      description: Skip interactive confirmation (required when stdin is not a TTY)
      attr: force

flair keys
  description: Manage Ed25519 key files in the key directory
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: prune

flair keys prune
  description: Move stale/unregistered/invalid keys to <keysDir>/.pruned/<date>/ — dry-run by default
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --apply
      description: Actually move prunable keys (default: dry-run, prints what would move and why)
      attr: apply
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory to scan for key files (else FLAIR_KEY_DIR, ~/.flair/keys)
      attr: keysDir
    --instance <url>
      description: Flair instance to check registration against (else FLAIR_TARGET/FLAIR_URL/config)
      attr: instance
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port (used when --instance/FLAIR_URL/FLAIR_TARGET are not set)
      attr: port

flair hook
  description: Manage ambient-memory harness SessionStart hooks (flair#745)
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: install, uninstall, status

flair hook install
  description: Wire the Flair SessionStart hook into the harness config so memory loads automatically at session start
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --harness <name>
      description: Target harness (claude-code, codex)
      attr: harness
      default: "claude-code"
    --dry-run
      description: Print the exact JSON delta without writing
      attr: dryRun
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID to wire (else FLAIR_AGENT_ID, else the agent already wired for this harness's MCP client)
      attr: agent
    --agent-id <id>
      description: Alias for --agent
      attr: agentId
    --url <url>
      description: Flair URL to wire (else FLAIR_TARGET/FLAIR_URL, else this harness's MCP wiring, else the local default)
      attr: url
    --continuity
      description: Wire the continuity capture hooks instead (PostToolUse + Stop — flair#1257; installing them IS the opt-in)
      attr: continuity

flair hook uninstall
  description: Remove the Flair SessionStart hook entry — only ours, everything else in the file is left untouched
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --harness <name>
      description: Target harness (claude-code, codex)
      attr: harness
      default: "claude-code"
    --dry-run
      description: Print the exact JSON delta without writing
      attr: dryRun
    --continuity
      description: Remove the continuity capture hooks instead (PostToolUse + Stop — flair#1257)
      attr: continuity

flair hook status
  description: Show whether the SessionStart hook is wired, its shape, and which Flair instance it targets
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --harness <name>
      description: Target harness (claude-code, codex)
      attr: harness
      default: "claude-code"

flair mcp
  description: MCP client-credentials agent-auth (RFC 7523 private_key_jwt)
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: token, grant, revoke, list, enable, disable, status

flair mcp token
  description: Build + sign an RFC 7523 client_assertion and request an MCP client_credentials access token. Caches the minted token (in-process) and reuses it until near-expiry — use --force-refresh to mint unconditionally.
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --agent-id <id>
      description: Agent id — becomes the client_id (iss/sub claims)
      attr: agentId
      mandatory: true
    --client-id <url>
      description: Client ID Metadata Document URL for this agent (defaults to this instance's MCPClientMetadata URL, derived from FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
      attr: clientId
    --token-endpoint <url>
      description: Token-endpoint URL — becomes the `aud` claim (defaults to this instance's own oauth token endpoint, same env vars)
      attr: tokenEndpoint
    --resource <url>
      description: RFC 8707 resource indicator for the token request (defaults to this instance's canonical /mcp URI)
      attr: resource
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory to look for <agentId>.key (else FLAIR_KEY_DIR, ~/.flair/keys, ~/.tps/secrets/flair)
      attr: keysDir
    --expires-in <seconds>
      description: Assertion exp - iat window, seconds (default + hard cap: 60)
      attr: expiresIn
    --dry-run
      description: Sign the assertion and print what would be sent, but do not call the token endpoint
      attr: dryRun
    --force-refresh
      description: Mint a fresh token even if a cached, not-near-expiry one exists
      attr: forceRefresh
    --json
      description: Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
      attr: json

flair mcp grant
  description: Provision a named, individually-revocable machine client for the /mcp OAuth surface (flair Agent + Ed25519 keypair; the existing CIMD path — see `flair mcp token` — makes it usable).
  usage: [options] <name>
  arguments:
    name (required)
  options:
    --issuer <url>
      description: Public origin for the CIMD client_id (defaults to FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
      attr: issuer
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory to write the new key pair into (else FLAIR_KEY_DIR, ~/.flair/keys)
      attr: keysDir
    --manifest <path>
      description: Path to the local machine-client manifest (else ~/.flair/mcp-clients.json)
      attr: manifest
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --json
      description: Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
      attr: json

flair mcp revoke
  description: Server-side revoke a granted machine client (deletes its backing Agent record), then clean up locally.
  usage: [options] <name>
  arguments:
    name (required)
  options:
    --manifest <path>
      description: Path to the local machine-client manifest (else ~/.flair/mcp-clients.json)
      attr: manifest
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --issuer <url>
      description: Public origin of the /mcp OAuth surface — used only for the enable-gate probe (defaults to FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
      attr: issuer
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --keep-keys
      description: Do not delete local key files after a successful server-side revoke
      attr: keepKeys

flair mcp list
  description: List granted machine clients (name, client_id, status, created).
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --manifest <path>
      description: Path to the local machine-client manifest (else ~/.flair/mcp-clients.json)
      attr: manifest
    --json
      description: Emit raw JSON array (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)
      attr: json

flair mcp enable
  description: One-command hosted-shape enablement of the OAuth /mcp surface for claude.ai — automates the docs/notes/mcp-oauth-model2.md checklist. Targets a REMOTE instance with a public HTTPS origin; refuses honestly against a local-origin instance.
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --instance <url>
      description: Remote flair instance to enable against (else FLAIR_URL)
      attr: instance
    --issuer <url>
      description: Public origin claude.ai will use (else --instance)
      attr: issuer
    --idp-provider <name>
      description: Upstream IdP provider
      attr: idpProvider
      default: "github"
    --idp-client-id <id>
      description: IdP OAuth app client id (else prompted interactively)
      attr: idpClientId
    --idp-client-secret <secret>
      description: IdP OAuth app client secret (else prompted interactively — prefer the prompt; an inline flag leaks to shell history)
      attr: idpClientSecret
    --idp-subject <value>
      description: Your expected `sub`/login at the IdP (GitHub: your username; else prompted interactively)
      attr: idpSubject
    --principal <id>
      description: Principal (Agent) to map your IdP identity to — personal-shape default
      attr: principal
      default: "self"
    --principal-kind <human|agent>
      description: Kind for a newly-created principal
      attr: principalKind
      default: "human"
    --secrets-mechanism <fabric-env-secrets|env-file>
      description: Override the shape-aware secrets mechanism (else auto-detected from --instance)
      attr: secretsMechanism
    --secrets-path <path>
      description: Override the secrets staging file path
      attr: secretsPath
    --cimd-allowed-hosts <hosts>
      description: Comma-separated clientIdMetadataDocuments.allowedHosts override (else claude.ai,claude.com)
      attr: cimdAllowedHosts
    --signing-key-file <path>
      description: RS256 signing key PEM file (else ~/.flair/mcp-signing-key.pem)
      attr: signingKeyFile
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password for the TARGET instance. Required explicitly for a remote target — FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS and ~/.flair/admin-pass are this machine's local credentials and are never sent to a remote instance
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --confirm-secrets-applied
      description: Confirm the staged secrets are already live on the target instance's environment (skips the interactive confirm)
      attr: confirmSecretsApplied
    --dry-run
      description: Generate keys/tokens/config and validate inputs; skip every remote call
      attr: dryRun
    --json
      description: Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
      attr: json

flair mcp disable
  description: Flag off + restart = byte-identical boot (Model-2 contract) — removes the /mcp OAuth surface.
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --instance <url>
      description: Remote flair instance to disable against (else FLAIR_URL)
      attr: instance
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password for the target instance (or FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --confirm-flag-off
      description: Confirm FLAIR_MCP_OAUTH is already unset on the target instance's environment (skips the interactive confirm)
      attr: confirmFlagOff
    --json
      description: Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
      attr: json

    --json

      attr: json

  usage: [options] <id>

      description: Grant admin privileges
      attr: admin
    --trust <tier>
      description: Default trust tier: endorsed, corroborated, or unverified
      attr: trust
    --runtime <runtime>
      description: Runtime: openclaw, claude-code, headless, external
      attr: runtime
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port

      description: Admin password for registration
      attr: adminPass

      attr: keysDir

      description: Harper operations API port

flair idp
  description: Manage enterprise IdP configurations (XAA)
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: add, list, remove, test

flair idp add
  description: Register a trusted enterprise IdP
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --name <name>
      description: Display name (e.g., 'Harper Corporate')
      attr: name
      mandatory: true
    --issuer <url>
      description: IdP issuer URL (e.g., https://accounts.google.com)
      attr: issuer
      mandatory: true
    --jwks-uri <url>
      description: JWKS endpoint URL
      attr: jwksUri
      mandatory: true
    --client-id <id>
      description: Flair's client_id at this IdP
      attr: clientId
      mandatory: true
    --required-domain <domain>
      description: Reject tokens without this domain (hd/tid claim)
      attr: requiredDomain
    --no-jit-provision
      description: Disable auto-creation of principals for new IdP users
      attr: jitProvision
      negate: true
    --default-trust <tier>
      description: Trust tier for JIT principals
      attr: defaultTrust
      default: "unverified"
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort

flair grant
  description: Grant an agent read access to another agent's memories
  usage: [options] <from-agent> <to-agent>
  arguments:
    from-agent (required)
    to-agent (required)
  options:
    --scope <scope>
      description: Grant scope: read or search
      attr: scope
      default: "read"
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Directory for Ed25519 keys (for from-agent Ed25519 auth)
      attr: keysDir

flair revoke
  description: Revoke a memory grant between two agents
  usage: [options] <from-agent> <to-agent>
  arguments:
    from-agent (required)
    to-agent (required)
  options:
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser

flair rem restore
  description: Restore from a REM snapshot (inspect by default; --apply rewinds Harper state)
  usage: [options] <date>
  arguments:
    date (required)
  options:
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use --admin-pass-file)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-pass-file <path>
      description: Read admin password from a file (e.g., ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and shell history.
      attr: adminPassFile
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent id (or FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
      attr: agent
    --target <dir>
      description: Directory to extract into (default: <snapshot>.restored, only used without --apply)
      attr: target
    --dry-run
      description: Plan-only — list contents or planned counts without writing
      attr: dryRun
    --apply
      description: Live replay: rewind Harper state to the snapshot (irreversible without the pre-restore snapshot)
      attr: apply

flair snapshot

  subcommands: create, list, restore

    --data-dir <path>
      description: Data directory to snapshot (default: ~/.flair/data)
      attr: dataDir

      attr: port

    --json
      description: Output as JSON

      attr: dataDir

      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --yes
      description: Skip the confirmation prompt (this destroys the current data directory)
      attr: yes

flair upgrade
  description: Upgrade Flair — local packages by default, or a deployed Fabric with --target
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --check
      description: Only check for updates / show the plan, don't install or deploy
      attr: check
    --tree <dir>
      description: Upgrade this extracted package tree in place (npm pack / plain-tree lane). Default: the serving instance's packed tree when that is not the npm-global install
      attr: tree
    --restart
      description: [deprecated] no-op — restart now happens automatically after upgrade; use --no-restart to opt out
      attr: restart
    --no-restart
      description: Skip the restart after upgrade (stage new packages now, restart later)
      attr: restart
      negate: true
    --no-verify
      description: Skip post-restart health/version/auth verification (default: verify — so a broken upgrade can't report success; see flair#635)
      attr: verify
      negate: true
    --snapshot
      description: Take a pre-upgrade ~/.flair/data snapshot before the package swap, keep-last-3 retention (default: off — see `flair snapshot create` to take one by hand, or `flair backup` for a logical export; flair#637)
      attr: snapshot
    --no-engine-snapshot
      description: Skip the pre-upgrade snapshot even when the Harper engine version is changing (flair#1047). The snapshot is automatic on engine-version changes because the tested-downgrade guarantee does not hold across engine boundaries. Opting out prints what is being given up.
      attr: engineSnapshot
      negate: true
    --all
      description: Show transitive packages (e.g. flair-client) in the listing — verbose mode for debugging dep versions
      attr: all
    --target <url>
      description: Upgrade the Flair deployed to this Fabric URL (not the local install)
      attr: target
    --fabric-user <user>
      description: Fabric admin username — for --target (env: FABRIC_USER preferred; inline leaks to shell history)
      attr: fabricUser
    --fabric-password <pass>
      description: Fabric admin password — for --target (prefer FABRIC_PASSWORD env or --fabric-password-file; inline leaks to shell history)
      attr: fabricPassword
    --fabric-password-file <path>
      description: Read the Fabric admin password from a file (chmod 600) — for --target
      attr: fabricPasswordFile
    --flair-version <semver>
      description: Flair version to deploy with --target, or to pin the plain-tree tarball swap (default: latest published @tpsdev-ai/flair)
      attr: flairVersion
    --harper-version <semver>
      description: Pin harper to this version for --target (default: registry latest, floored at the flair#513 fix)
      attr: harperVersion
    --project <name>
      description: Fabric component name for --target
      attr: project
      default: "flair"
    --no-replicated
      description: Disable cluster-wide replication for --target (default: replicated=true)
      attr: replicated
      negate: true
    --yes
      description: Skip the confirmation prompt for --target
      attr: yes
    --install-hooks
      description: Consent to installing missing SessionStart hooks (claude-code / Codex) during upgrade. The hook executes at every session start — upgrade will not write it unprompted. Interactive runs prompt; non-interactive runs state the gap and withhold ✅ unless this flag is passed.
      attr: installHooks
    --no-fleet-verify
      description: Skip the automatic post-upgrade fleet convergence sweep for --target (default: sweep runs — see flair#636)
      attr: fleetVerify
      negate: true
    --deploy-retries <n>
      description: Retry the full harper deploy this many times for --target, ONLY when peer replication is positively observed not to converge (default: 0 — a retry can escalate a transient replication warning into a hard install failure; see flair#878)
      attr: deployRetries
      default: "0"
    --ignore-replication-errors
      description: For --target: if peer replication still hasn't converged, accept an origin-only deploy instead of failing (the peer catches up via federation sync or a later deploy)
      attr: ignoreReplicationErrors
    --no-convergence-check
      description: For --target: skip the post-replication-error convergence poll and fail on harper's error verbatim (default: poll — Harper replicates asynchronously, so its error is a snapshot, not a verdict; flair#878)
      attr: convergenceCheck
      negate: true
    --convergence-timeout <ms>
      description: For --target: how long to wait for peer replication to converge before reporting a replication failure (default: 180000)
      attr: convergenceTimeout

flair reembed
  description: Re-generate embeddings for memories with stale or missing model tags
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID to re-embed memories for (defaults to all agents with stale rows)
      attr: agent
    --stale-only
      description: Only re-embed memories with mismatched model tag
      attr: staleOnly
    --dry-run
      description: Show count without modifying
      attr: dryRun
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --batch-size <n>
      description: Records per batch
      attr: batchSize
      default: "50"
    --delay-ms <ms>
      description: Delay between batches (ms)
      attr: delayMs
      default: "100"

flair deploy
  description: Deploy Flair as a component to a remote Harper Fabric cluster
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --fabric-org <org>
      description: Fabric org (env: FABRIC_ORG)
      attr: fabricOrg
    --fabric-cluster <cluster>
      description: Fabric cluster within the org (env: FABRIC_CLUSTER)
      attr: fabricCluster
    --fabric-user <user>
      description: Fabric admin username (env: FABRIC_USER preferred; inline leaks to shell history)
      attr: fabricUser
    --fabric-password <pass>
      description: Fabric admin password (prefer FABRIC_PASSWORD env or --fabric-password-file; inline leaks to shell history)
      attr: fabricPassword
    --fabric-password-file <path>
      description: Read the Fabric admin password from a file (chmod 600)
      attr: fabricPasswordFile
    --fabric-token <token>
      description: OAuth bearer token (env: FABRIC_TOKEN) — reserved for future Fabric bearer support
      attr: fabricToken
    --target <url>
      description: Override the Fabric URL template (https://<cluster>.<org>.harperfabric.com)
      attr: target
    --project <name>
      description: Component name in Fabric
      attr: project
      default: "flair"
    --pkg-version <semver>
      description: Override version label (default: installed package version)
      attr: pkgVersion
    --no-replicated
      description: Disable cluster-wide replication (default: replicated=true)
      attr: replicated
      negate: true
    --no-restart
      description: Do not restart the component after deploy (default: restart=true)
      attr: restart
      negate: true
    --dry-run
      description: Resolve package, validate args, skip the deploy call
      attr: dryRun
    --package-root <dir>
      description: Override package root (mainly for testing)
      attr: packageRoot
    --deployment-timeout <ms>
      description: Milliseconds harper waits for cluster-wide peer replication (env: FABRIC_DEPLOYMENT_TIMEOUT; default: 600000 — harper's own 120s default is too short for Fabric)
      attr: deploymentTimeout
    --install-timeout <ms>
      description: Milliseconds harper waits for package install (env: FABRIC_INSTALL_TIMEOUT; default: 600000)
      attr: installTimeout
    --no-verify
      description: Skip post-deploy served-API verification (default: verify — on by design, so the CLI can't report success on an empty/broken deploy)
      attr: verify
      negate: true
    --verify-timeout <ms>
      description: Milliseconds to wait for the served API to settle after harper's post-deploy restart before verifying (default: 300000)
      attr: verifyTimeout
    --verify-resource <name>
      description: Resource to verify is serving after deploy (repeatable; default: derived from the deployed package's dist/resources)
      attr: verifyResource
      default: []
    --deploy-retries <n>
      description: Retry the full harper deploy this many times, ONLY when peer replication is positively observed not to converge (default: 0 — retrying re-runs harper's component install and can escalate a transient replication warning into a hard ENOTEMPTY install failure; see flair#878)
      attr: deployRetries
      default: "0"
    --ignore-replication-errors
      description: If peer replication still hasn't converged, treat it as a non-fatal warning and succeed with an origin-only deploy (the peer catches up via federation sync or a later deploy)
      attr: ignoreReplicationErrors
    --no-convergence-check
      description: Skip the post-replication-error convergence poll and fail on harper's error verbatim (default: poll — Harper replicates asynchronously, so its error is a snapshot, not a verdict; flair#878)
      attr: convergenceCheck
      negate: true
    --convergence-timeout <ms>
      description: How long to wait for peer replication to converge before reporting a replication failure (default: 180000)
      attr: convergenceTimeout
    --no-fleet-verify
      description: Skip the automatic post-deploy fleet convergence sweep (default: sweep runs — see flair#636)
      attr: fleetVerify
      negate: true

flair fleet verify
  description: Sweep a Fabric origin + its known federation peers for version/health convergence
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --target <url>
      description: Fabric URL to verify (the origin node)
      attr: target
      mandatory: true
    --fabric-user <user>
      description: Fabric admin username (env: FABRIC_USER — preferred; inline leaks to ps/shell history)
      attr: fabricUser
    --fabric-password <pass>
      description: Fabric admin password (prefer FABRIC_PASSWORD env or --fabric-password-file; inline leaks to shell history)
      attr: fabricPassword
    --fabric-password-file <path>
      description: Read the Fabric admin password from a mode-0600 file (keeps it out of argv and env)
      attr: fabricPasswordFile
    --expect-version <semver>
      description: Version every node must report (default: the origin's own reported version — a self-consistency check)
      attr: expectVersion
    --timeout <ms>
      description: Per-node /Health poll timeout in ms
      attr: timeout
      default: "60000"
    --json
      description: Emit JSON (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)
      attr: json

      attr: port

      attr: target

      description: Output as JSON

    --emit

Requires an agent identity (--agent or FLAIR_AGENT_ID) — the opt-in write boundary; without this flag `flair quality` remains fully read-only
      attr: emit

flair memory
  description: Manage agent memories
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: add, write-task-summary, search, basement, restore, list, hygiene

flair memory add
  description: Write a new memory row for an agent (content via positional arg or --content)
  usage: [options] [content]
  arguments:
    content (optional)
  options:
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID (or set FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
      attr: agent
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use --admin-pass-file)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-pass-file <path>
      description: Read admin password from a file (e.g., ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and shell history.
      attr: adminPassFile
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --content <text>
      description: memory content (alias for positional arg)
      attr: content
    --durability <d>
      description: permanent|persistent|standard|ephemeral (default standard). Also decides the default visibility when --visibility is omitted: permanent/persistent -> shared, standard/ephemeral -> private
      attr: durability
    --tags <csv>
      attr: tags
    --summary <text>
      description: agent-set multi-sentence dense compression (3-tier chain: subject → summary → content)
      attr: summary
    --subject <text>
      description: one-line title / entity this memory is about
      attr: subject
    --derived-from <csv>
      description: Comma-separated source Memory IDs this memory was distilled/reflected from (sets Memory.derivedFrom; used by the `rem rapid` reflection loop)
      attr: derivedFrom
    --visibility <value>
      description: Writer-controlled sharing intent (sets Memory.visibility): 'private' (owner-only, never visible to any other agent) or 'shared' (visible to owner + every other agent on this instance — open within the org, not gated by a MemoryGrant). Omit to use the server's durability-keyed default: permanent/persistent -> shared, standard/ephemeral -> private (flair#509)
      attr: visibility
    --entities <csv>
      description: Comma-separated entity vocabulary strings this record touches (type:value from the closed type set, e.g. repo:tpsdev-ai/flair — see docs/entity-vocabulary.md; feeds `flair attention`)
      attr: entities

flair search
  description: Search memories by meaning (shortcut for memory search) — filterable, with --explain ranking
  usage: [options] <query>
  arguments:
    query (required)
  options:
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID (or set FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
      attr: agent
    --limit <n>
      description: Max results
      attr: limit
      default: "5"
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --url <url>
      description: Flair base URL (overrides --port)
      attr: url
    --target <url>
      description: Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET; alias for --url)
      attr: target
    --key <path>
      description: Ed25519 private key path
      attr: key
    --tag <tag>
      description: Filter to memories carrying this tag
      attr: tag
    --subject <subject>
      description: Filter to memories carrying this subject (case-insensitive)
      attr: subject
    --subjects <list>
      description: Comma-separated list of subjects to OR-filter (case-insensitive)
      attr: subjects
    --since <iso-or-relative>
      description: Only memories created after this point (ISO 8601 or '7d'/'24h'/'30m')
      attr: since
    --as-of <iso>
      description: Temporal validity: only memories valid at this point (ISO 8601)
      attr: asOf
    --include-superseded
      description: Include memories that have been superseded
      attr: includeSuperseded
    --scoring <mode>
      description: Scoring mode: raw (default) uses cosine similarity/BM25 only; composite re-ranks by durability/recency/retrieval (measurably hurts precision as of flair#623 — opt-in only)
      attr: scoring
      default: "raw"
    --min-score <n>
      description: Drop results below this score (0..1)
      attr: minScore
      default: "0"
    --durability <level>
      description: Filter to permanent|persistent|standard|ephemeral (client-side)
      attr: durability
    --source <name>
      description: Filter by source/agentId (client-side)
      attr: source
    --explain
      description: Show score breakdown (raw, composite, durability, age, usage) per hit — also added to --json output as _explain
      attr: explain
    --json
      description: Output raw JSON array
      attr: json

flair relationship
  description: Manage agent relationship triples (knowledge graph)
  usage: [options] [command]
  options: (none)
  subcommands: add

flair relationship add
  description: Record that <subject> <predicate> <object> — an explicit entity-to-entity relationship triple. Re-asserting the SAME triple (same subject/predicate/object) UPSERTS the existing row rather than duplicating it. Predicate is free text; recommended vocabulary: manages, works_on, reviews, depends_on, replaces, owns, reports_to, advises. To CONTRADICT a prior relationship: changing the predicate creates a SEPARATE row and does NOT auto-close the old one — re-assert the OLD triple with --valid-to set to now (or delete it) before/after writing the new one.
  usage: [options]
  options:
    --agent <id>
      attr: agent
      mandatory: true
    --subject <text>
      description: Source entity (e.g. 'nathan')
      attr: subject
      mandatory: true
    --predicate <text>
      description: Relationship type, free text (e.g. 'manages')
      attr: predicate
      mandatory: true
    --object <text>
      description: Target entity (e.g. 'flair')
      attr: object
      mandatory: true
    --confidence <n>
      description: 0.0-1.0, how certain (default 1.0 = explicitly stated)
      attr: confidence
    --valid-from <iso>
      description: ISO timestamp this relationship became true (default: now)
      attr: validFrom
    --valid-to <iso>
      description: ISO timestamp this relationship ended (leave unset for an active relationship)
      attr: validTo
    --source <text>
      description: Where this was learned from (a memory ID, conversation, etc.)
      attr: source

flair export
  description: Export a single agent's identity (soul + memories) to a portable file
  usage: [options] <agent-id>
  arguments:
    agent-id (required)
  options:
    --output <path>
      description: Output file path
      attr: output
    --include-key
      description: Include private key in export (UNENCRYPTED — keep the output file secure)
      attr: includeKey
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --url <url>
      description: Flair base URL (overrides --port)
      attr: url
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Keys directory
      attr: keysDir
      default: "~/.flair/keys"

flair import
  description: Import an agent from an export file into this Flair instance
  usage: [options] <path>
  arguments:
    path (required)
  options:
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --ops-port <port>
      description: Harper operations API port
      attr: opsPort
    --url <url>
      description: Flair base URL (overrides --port)
      attr: url
    --ops-target <url>
      description: Explicit ops API URL for the Agent seed (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET; bypasses port derivation). Use when --url is remote and the ops port isn't HTTP-1.
      attr: opsTarget
    --admin-pass <pass>
      description: Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env)
      attr: adminPass
    --admin-user <name>
      description: Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
      attr: adminUser
    --keys-dir <dir>
      description: Keys directory
      attr: keysDir
      default: "~/.flair/keys"

  options:
    --json
      description: Emit raw JSON of the file (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)
      attr: json

      attr: summary
      mandatory: true
    --detail <text>
      description: Longer detail payload
      attr: detail

      description: Scope of the event (e.g. an agent id, repo, or 'org')
      attr: scope
    --target <agentId>
      description: Recipient agent id (repeatable)
      attr: target
      default: []
    --entities <csv>
      description: Comma-separated entity vocabulary strings this record touches (type:value from the closed type set, e.g. repo:tpsdev-ai/flair — see docs/entity-vocabulary.md; feeds `flair attention`)
      attr: entities
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID (env: FLAIR_AGENT_ID)
      attr: agent

      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --target-url <url>
      description: Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
      attr: targetUrl

flair attention
  description: What's touching entity E in the last N days? Grouped view across memory/relationship/workspace/presence/orgevent (POST /AttentionQuery)
  usage: [options] <entity>
  arguments:
    entity (required)
  options:
    --days <n>
      description: Window size in days (default 7)
      attr: days
    --agent <id>
      description: Agent ID (or set FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
      attr: agent
    --key <path>
      description: Ed25519 private key path
      attr: key
    --port <port>
      description: Harper HTTP port
      attr: port
    --url <url>
      description: Flair base URL (overrides --port)
      attr: url
    --target <url>
      description: Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET; alias for --url)
      attr: target
    --json
      description: Output raw JSON
      attr: json

HELP

----- flair -----
Usage: flair [options] [command]

Options:
  -v, --version                             output the version number
  -h, --help                                display help for command

Commands:
  init [options]                            One-command Flair setup — bootstrap the instance, register an agent, and wire MCP clients
  agent                                     Manage Flair agents
  keys                                      Manage Ed25519 key files in the key directory
  hook                                      Manage ambient-memory harness SessionStart hooks (flair#745)
  mcp                                       MCP client-credentials agent-auth (RFC 7523 private_key_jwt)
  principal                                 Manage principals (humans and agents)
  idp                                       Manage enterprise IdP configurations (XAA)
  grant [options] <from-agent> <to-agent>   Grant an agent read access to another agent's memories
  revoke [options] <from-agent> <to-agent>  Revoke a memory grant between two agents
  federation                                Manage federation (hub-and-spoke sync)
  rem                                       Memory hygiene and reflection
  status [options]                          Show Flair instance status, memory stats, and agent info
  snapshot                                  Physical ~/.flair/data snapshots (byte-exact tar.gz, local-only — see `flair backup`/`flair restore` for the logical JSON export/import)
  upgrade [options]                         Upgrade Flair — local packages by default, or a deployed Fabric with --target
  stop [options]                            Stop the running Flair (Harper) instance
  start [options]                           Start Flair (Harper) — requires a prior 'flair init'
  restart [options]                         Restart the Flair (Harper) instance
  uninstall [options]                       Stop Flair and remove the launchd/systemd service
  reembed [options]                         Re-generate embeddings for memories with stale or missing model tags
  test [options]                            Verify the full Flair stack: write, search, and delete a test memory
  deploy [options]                          Deploy Flair as a component to a remote Harper Fabric cluster
  fleet                                     Fabric fleet operations (post-deploy convergence verification)
  doctor [options]                          Diagnose common Flair problems and suggest fixes
  quality [options]                         Memory-quality report: embedding coverage, staleness, signal density, quiet agents, recall spot-check (read-only)
  session                                   Agent session lifecycle (snapshot/restore for FLAIR-AGENT-CONTEXT-TIERS-B)
  memory                                    Manage agent memories
  search [options] <query>                  Search memories by meaning (shortcut for memory search) — filterable, with --explain ranking
  bootstrap [options]                       Cold-start context: get soul + recent memories as formatted text
  relationship                              Manage agent relationship triples (knowledge graph)
  soul                                      Manage agent soul entries
  bridge                                    Manage memory bridges (import/export between Flair and foreign systems)
  backup [options]                          Export agents, memories, and souls to a JSON archive
  restore [options] <path>                  Import a Flair backup archive
  export [options] <agent-id>               Export a single agent's identity (soul + memories) to a portable file
  import [options] <path>                   Import an agent from an export file into this Flair instance
  inspect [options] <path>                  Show contents of a backup or export file
  migrate-harness-memory [options]          Migrate harness-local memories to Flair
  presence                                  Manage agent presence (The Office Space)
  workspace                                 Manage agent workspace state (The Office Space)
  orgevent [options]                        Publish an org-wide coordination event attributed to your agent (PUT /OrgEvent/{id})
  attention [options] <entity>              What's touching entity E in the last N days? Grouped view across memory/relationship/workspace/presence/orgevent (POST /AttentionQuery)
  help [command]                            display help for command

----- flair init -----
Usage: flair init [options]

One-command Flair setup — bootstrap the instance, register an agent, and wire
MCP clients

Options:
  --agent-id <id>              Agent ID to register (omit to bootstrap instance
                               without agent)
  --agent <id>                 Alias for --agent-id
  --port <port>                Harper HTTP port (default: this instance's
                               current port, or 19926 for a new one)
  --ops-port <port>            Harper operations API port
  --ops-bind <addr>            Harper ops API bind address (env: FLAIR_OPS_BIND;
                               default: 127.0.0.1 loopback-only for single-host
                               — pass e.g. 0.0.0.0 for multi-host/Fabric remote
                               admin)
  --admin-pass <pass>          Admin password (generated if omitted)
  --admin-pass-file <path>     Read admin password from file (chmod 600
                               recommended)
  --admin-user <name>          Admin username when authenticating to an
                               already-running instance via
                               --target/--ops-target (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER;
                               default: admin — local bootstrap and Fabric
                               provisioning always create 'admin')
  --keys-dir <dir>             Directory for Ed25519 keys
  --data-dir <dir>             Harper data directory
  --skip-start                 Skip Harper startup (assume already running)
  --skip-soul                  Skip interactive personality setup
  --client <client>            Client(s) to wire: claude-code, codex, gemini,
                               cursor, antigravity, pi (native extension), all,
                               or none
  --no-mcp                     Skip MCP client wiring (instance + agent only)
  --skip-smoke                 Skip the MCP smoke test
  --skip-claude-md             Skip appending the Flair bootstrap line to
                               CLAUDE.md (claude-code only)
  --skip-hook                  Skip installing the flair-session-start
                               SessionStart hook (claude-code and Codex)
  --target <url>               Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
  --remote                     When used with --target, init as hub for remote
                               federation
  --ops-target <url>           Explicit ops API URL (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET;
                               bypasses port derivation)
  --force                      Skip confirmation prompt for remote writes
                               (required with --target)
  --cluster-admin-user <user>  Harper cluster admin username (env:
                               FLAIR_CLUSTER_ADMIN_USER)
  --cluster-admin-pass <pass>  Harper cluster admin password (env:
                               FLAIR_CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASS)
  --flair-admin-pass <pass>    Password for Flair's admin user (env:
                               FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS; generated if omitted)
  -h, --help                   display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                output the version number

----- flair agent -----
Usage: flair agent [options] [command]

Manage Flair agents

Options:
  -h, --help                 display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version              output the version number

Commands:
  add [options] <id>         Register a new agent in a running Flair instance
  list [options]             List all agents
  show [options] <id>        Show agent details
  rotate-key [options] <id>  Rotate an agent's Ed25519 keypair
  remove [options] <id>      Remove an agent and all its data from Flair
  help [command]             display help for command

----- flair agent add -----
Usage: flair agent add [options] <id>

Register a new agent in a running Flair instance

Options:
  --name <name>             Display name (defaults to id)
  --port <port>             Harper HTTP port
  --admin-pass <pass>       Admin password for registration
  --admin-pass-file <path>  Read the admin password from a file (chmod 600
                            enforced). Preferred over inline --admin-pass —
                            keeps the secret out of ps and shell history; works
                            for remote targets too (an explicit flag is operator
                            intent).
  --admin-user <name>       Admin username for Basic auth (env:
                            FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  --keys-dir <dir>          Directory for Ed25519 keys
  --ops-port <port>         Harper operations API port
  --target <url>            Remote Flair REST URL; derives the ops API URL
                            (port-1) to seed the Agent there (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
  --ops-target <url>        Explicit ops API URL to seed the Agent on (env:
                            FLAIR_OPS_TARGET; bypasses port derivation)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version             output the version number

----- flair mcp -----
Usage: flair mcp [options] [command]

MCP client-credentials agent-auth (RFC 7523 private_key_jwt)

Options:
  -h, --help               display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version            output the version number

Commands:
  token [options]          Build + sign an RFC 7523 client_assertion and request
                           an MCP client_credentials access token. Caches the
                           minted token (in-process) and reuses it until
                           near-expiry — use --force-refresh to mint
                           unconditionally.
  grant [options] <name>   Provision a named, individually-revocable machine
                           client for the /mcp OAuth surface (flair Agent +
                           Ed25519 keypair; the existing CIMD path — see `flair
                           mcp token` — makes it usable).
  revoke [options] <name>  Server-side revoke a granted machine client (deletes
                           its backing Agent record), then clean up locally.
  list [options]           List granted machine clients (name, client_id,
                           status, created).
  enable [options]         One-command hosted-shape enablement of the OAuth /mcp
                           surface for claude.ai — automates the
                           docs/notes/mcp-oauth-model2.md checklist. Targets a
                           REMOTE instance with a public HTTPS origin; refuses
                           honestly against a local-origin instance.
  disable [options]        Flag off + restart = byte-identical boot (Model-2
                           contract) — removes the /mcp OAuth surface.
  status [options]         Surface the /mcp OAuth surface's live state: enabled?
                           CIMD advertised? granted machine-client count.
  help [command]           display help for command

----- flair mcp token -----
Usage: flair mcp token [options]

Build + sign an RFC 7523 client_assertion and request an MCP client_credentials
access token. Caches the minted token (in-process) and reuses it until
near-expiry — use --force-refresh to mint unconditionally.

Options:
  --agent-id <id>         Agent id — becomes the client_id (iss/sub claims)
  --client-id <url>       Client ID Metadata Document URL for this agent
                          (defaults to this instance's MCPClientMetadata URL,
                          derived from FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
  --token-endpoint <url>  Token-endpoint URL — becomes the `aud` claim (defaults
                          to this instance's own oauth token endpoint, same env
                          vars)
  --resource <url>        RFC 8707 resource indicator for the token request
                          (defaults to this instance's canonical /mcp URI)
  --keys-dir <dir>        Directory to look for <agentId>.key (else
                          FLAIR_KEY_DIR, ~/.flair/keys, ~/.tps/secrets/flair)
  --expires-in <seconds>  Assertion exp - iat window, seconds (default + hard
                          cap: 60)
  --dry-run               Sign the assertion and print what would be sent, but
                          do not call the token endpoint
  --force-refresh         Mint a fresh token even if a cached, not-near-expiry
                          one exists
  --json                  Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
  -h, --help              display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version           output the version number

----- flair mcp grant -----
Usage: flair mcp grant [options] <name>

Provision a named, individually-revocable machine client for the /mcp OAuth
surface (flair Agent + Ed25519 keypair; the existing CIMD path — see `flair mcp
token` — makes it usable).

Options:
  --issuer <url>       Public origin for the CIMD client_id (defaults to
                       FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
  --keys-dir <dir>     Directory to write the new key pair into (else
                       FLAIR_KEY_DIR, ~/.flair/keys)
  --manifest <path>    Path to the local machine-client manifest (else
                       ~/.flair/mcp-clients.json)
  --admin-pass <pass>  Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS)
  --admin-user <name>  Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER;
                       default: admin)
  --port <port>        Harper HTTP port
  --ops-port <port>    Harper operations API port
  --json               Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
  -h, --help           display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version        output the version number

----- flair mcp revoke -----
Usage: flair mcp revoke [options] <name>

Server-side revoke a granted machine client (deletes its backing Agent record),
then clean up locally.

Options:
  --manifest <path>    Path to the local machine-client manifest (else
                       ~/.flair/mcp-clients.json)
  --admin-pass <pass>  Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS)
  --admin-user <name>  Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER;
                       default: admin)
  --issuer <url>       Public origin of the /mcp OAuth surface — used only for
                       the enable-gate probe (defaults to
                       FLAIR_MCP_ISSUER/FLAIR_PUBLIC_URL)
  --ops-port <port>    Harper operations API port
  --port <port>        Harper HTTP port
  --keep-keys          Do not delete local key files after a successful
                       server-side revoke
  -h, --help           display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version        output the version number

  --json             Emit raw JSON array (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)

----- flair mcp enable -----
Usage: flair mcp enable [options]

One-command hosted-shape enablement of the OAuth /mcp surface for claude.ai —
automates the docs/notes/mcp-oauth-model2.md checklist. Targets a REMOTE
instance with a public HTTPS origin; refuses honestly against a local-origin
instance.

Options:
  --instance <url>                                   Remote flair instance to enable against (else FLAIR_URL)
  --issuer <url>                                     Public origin claude.ai will use (else --instance)
  --idp-provider <name>                              Upstream IdP provider (default: "github")
  --idp-client-id <id>                               IdP OAuth app client id (else prompted interactively)
  --idp-client-secret <secret>                       IdP OAuth app client secret (else prompted interactively — prefer the prompt; an inline flag leaks to shell history)
  --idp-subject <value>                              Your expected `sub`/login at the IdP (GitHub: your username; else prompted interactively)
  --principal <id>                                   Principal (Agent) to map your IdP identity to — personal-shape default (default: "self")
  --principal-kind <human|agent>                     Kind for a newly-created principal (default: "human")
  --secrets-mechanism <fabric-env-secrets|env-file>  Override the shape-aware secrets mechanism (else auto-detected from --instance)
  --secrets-path <path>                              Override the secrets staging file path
  --cimd-allowed-hosts <hosts>                       Comma-separated clientIdMetadataDocuments.allowedHosts override (else claude.ai,claude.com)
  --signing-key-file <path>                          RS256 signing key PEM file (else ~/.flair/mcp-signing-key.pem)
  --admin-pass <pass>                                Admin password for the TARGET instance. Required explicitly for a remote target — FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS and ~/.flair/admin-pass are this machine's local credentials and are never sent to a remote instance
  --admin-user <name>                                Admin username for Basic auth (env: FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  --confirm-secrets-applied                          Confirm the staged secrets are already live on the target instance's environment (skips the interactive confirm)
  --dry-run                                          Generate keys/tokens/config and validate inputs; skip every remote call
  --json                                             Print machine-readable JSON instead of a human summary
  -h, --help                                         display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                                      output the version number

----- flair federation -----
Usage: flair federation [options] [command]

Manage federation (hub-and-spoke sync)

Options:
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version             output the version number

Commands:
  status [options]          Show federation status and peer connections
  reachability [options]    Probe local Flair + each paired peer for
                            reachability (read-only)
  pair [options] <hub-url>  Pair this spoke with a hub instance
  token [options]           Generate a one-time pairing token (run on the hub)
  sync [options]            Push local changes to the hub (one-shot).
                            Subcommands manage the scheduled driver.
  watch [options]           Run federation sync in a loop (foreground daemon)
  prune [options]           Remove stale spoke peers (older than --older-than).
                            Hub is never pruned. Default dry-run.
  verify [options]          End-to-end check: write a tagged memory, push it,
                            and verify it shows up on each peer
  help [command]            display help for command

----- flair federation sync -----
Usage: flair federation sync [options] [command]

Push local changes to the hub (one-shot). Subcommands manage the scheduled
driver.

Options:
  --port <port>             Harper HTTP port
  --ops-port <port>         Harper operations API port
  --target <url>            Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
  --ops-target <url>        Explicit ops API URL (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET;
                            bypasses port derivation)
  --admin-pass <pass>       Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use
                            --admin-pass-file)
  --admin-pass-file <path>  Read admin password from a file (e.g.,
                            ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass
                            for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and
                            shell history.
  --admin-user <name>       Admin username for Basic auth (env:
                            FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version             output the version number

  enable [options]          Install the sync driver (launchd on macOS, systemd
                            timer on Linux)
  disable [options]         Remove the sync driver (peers and sync history are
                            preserved)
  status [options]          Show whether a sync driver is installed and
                            genuinely active

----- flair federation sync enable -----

Install the sync driver (launchd on macOS, systemd timer on Linux)

  --interval <seconds>      Seconds between syncs (default 300) (default: "300")
  --no-credentials          Do not wire any credential file into the unit
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  --port <port>             Harper HTTP port
  --ops-port <port>         Harper operations API port
  --target <url>            Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET)
  --ops-target <url>        Explicit ops API URL (env: FLAIR_OPS_TARGET;
                            bypasses port derivation)
  --admin-pass <pass>       Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use
                            --admin-pass-file)
  --admin-pass-file <path>  Read admin password from a file (e.g.,
                            ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass
                            for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and
                            shell history.
  --admin-user <name>       Admin username for Basic auth (env:
                            FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  -v, --version             output the version number

Credentials:
  --admin-pass-file defaults to ~/.flair/admin-pass when that file exists.
  The PATH is stored in the unit — never the password.

----- flair rem -----
Usage: flair rem [options] [command]

Memory hygiene and reflection

Options:
  -h, --help                        display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                     output the version number

Commands:
  light [options]                   NREM — quick cleanup: delete expired,
                                    archive old, consolidate candidates
  rapid [options]                   REM — reflection/learning: distill recent
                                    memories into staged candidates
  restorative [options]             Deep audit: full maintenance + consolidation
                                    (olderThan=7d) + reflection
  candidates [options]              List staged memory candidates from the
                                    FLAIR-NIGHTLY-REM cycle (pending review)
  promote [options] <candidate-id>  Promote a memory candidate to Soul or
                                    persistent Memory (rationale required)
  reject [options] <candidate-id>   Reject a memory candidate with a required
                                    reason
  nightly                           Scheduled REM nightly cycle (manual trigger
                                    + scheduler management)
  snapshot                          REM nightly snapshots (tar.gz archives of
                                    agent memory + soul)
  restore [options] <date>          Restore from a REM snapshot (inspect by
                                    default; --apply rewinds Harper state)
  pause                             Pause nightly REM runs and abort an
                                    in-flight distillation gather
  abort                             Abort an in-flight REM distillation (same
                                    sentinel as pause)
  resume                            Resume nightly REM runs — removes the pause
                                    sentinel
  help [command]                    display help for command

----- flair rem nightly enable -----
Usage: flair rem nightly enable [options]

Install the nightly scheduler (launchd on macOS, systemd timer on Linux)

Options:
  --agent <id>       Agent id (or FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
  --at <HH:MM>       Local time to run nightly (default 03:00) (default:
                     "03:00")
  --flair-url <url>  Flair HTTP URL the runner will hit (default
                     http://127.0.0.1:<port>)
  -h, --help         display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version      output the version number

----- flair rem restore -----
Usage: flair rem restore [options] <date>

Restore from a REM snapshot (inspect by default; --apply rewinds Harper state)

Options:
  --admin-pass <pass>       Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use
                            --admin-pass-file)
  --admin-pass-file <path>  Read admin password from a file (e.g.,
                            ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass
                            for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and
                            shell history.
  --admin-user <name>       Admin username for Basic auth (env:
                            FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  --agent <id>              Agent id (or FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
  --target <dir>            Directory to extract into (default:
                            <snapshot>.restored, only used without --apply)
  --dry-run                 Plan-only — list contents or planned counts without
                            writing
  --apply                   Live replay: rewind Harper state to the snapshot
                            (irreversible without the pre-restore snapshot)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version             output the version number

----- flair upgrade -----
Usage: flair upgrade [options]

Upgrade Flair — local packages by default, or a deployed Fabric with --target

Options:
  --check                        Only check for updates / show the plan, don't
                                 install or deploy
  --tree <dir>                   Upgrade this extracted package tree in place
                                 (npm pack / plain-tree lane). Default: the
                                 serving instance's packed tree when that is not
                                 the npm-global install
  --restart                      [deprecated] no-op — restart now happens
                                 automatically after upgrade; use --no-restart
                                 to opt out
  --no-restart                   Skip the restart after upgrade (stage new
                                 packages now, restart later)
  --no-verify                    Skip post-restart health/version/auth
                                 verification (default: verify — so a broken
                                 upgrade can't report success; see flair#635)
  --snapshot                     Take a pre-upgrade ~/.flair/data snapshot
                                 before the package swap, keep-last-3 retention
                                 (default: off — see `flair snapshot create` to
                                 take one by hand, or `flair backup` for a
                                 logical export; flair#637)
  --no-engine-snapshot           Skip the pre-upgrade snapshot even when the
                                 Harper engine version is changing (flair#1047).
                                 The snapshot is automatic on engine-version
                                 changes because the tested-downgrade guarantee
                                 does not hold across engine boundaries. Opting
                                 out prints what is being given up.
  --all                          Show transitive packages (e.g. flair-client) in
                                 the listing — verbose mode for debugging dep
                                 versions
  --target <url>                 Upgrade the Flair deployed to this Fabric URL
                                 (not the local install)
  --fabric-user <user>           Fabric admin username — for --target (env:
                                 FABRIC_USER preferred; inline leaks to shell
                                 history)
  --fabric-password <pass>       Fabric admin password — for --target (prefer
                                 FABRIC_PASSWORD env or --fabric-password-file;
                                 inline leaks to shell history)
  --fabric-password-file <path>  Read the Fabric admin password from a file
                                 (chmod 600) — for --target
  --flair-version <semver>       Flair version to deploy with --target, or to
                                 pin the plain-tree tarball swap (default:
                                 latest published @tpsdev-ai/flair)
  --harper-version <semver>      Pin harper to this version for --target
                                 (default: registry latest, floored at the
                                 flair#513 fix)
  --project <name>               Fabric component name for --target (default:
                                 "flair")
  --no-replicated                Disable cluster-wide replication for --target
                                 (default: replicated=true)
  --yes                          Skip the confirmation prompt for --target
  --install-hooks                Consent to installing missing SessionStart
                                 hooks (claude-code / Codex) during upgrade. The
                                 hook executes at every session start — upgrade
                                 will not write it unprompted. Interactive runs
                                 prompt; non-interactive runs state the gap and
                                 withhold ✅ unless this flag is passed.
  --no-fleet-verify              Skip the automatic post-upgrade fleet
                                 convergence sweep for --target (default: sweep
                                 runs — see flair#636)
  --deploy-retries <n>           Retry the full harper deploy this many times
                                 for --target, ONLY when peer replication is
                                 positively observed not to converge (default: 0
                                 — a retry can escalate a transient replication
                                 warning into a hard install failure; see
                                 flair#878) (default: "0")
  --ignore-replication-errors    For --target: if peer replication still hasn't
                                 converged, accept an origin-only deploy instead
                                 of failing (the peer catches up via federation
                                 sync or a later deploy)
  --no-convergence-check         For --target: skip the post-replication-error
                                 convergence poll and fail on harper's error
                                 verbatim (default: poll — Harper replicates
                                 asynchronously, so its error is a snapshot, not
                                 a verdict; flair#878)
  --convergence-timeout <ms>     For --target: how long to wait for peer
                                 replication to converge before reporting a
                                 replication failure (default: 180000)
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                  output the version number
