----- flair deploy -----
Usage: flair deploy [options]

Deploy Flair as a component to a remote Harper Fabric cluster

Options:
  --fabric-org <org>             Fabric org (env: FABRIC_ORG)
  --fabric-cluster <cluster>     Fabric cluster within the org (env:
                                 FABRIC_CLUSTER)
  --fabric-user <user>           Fabric admin username (env: FABRIC_USER
                                 preferred; inline leaks to shell history)
  --fabric-password <pass>       Fabric admin password (prefer FABRIC_PASSWORD
                                 env or --fabric-password-file; inline leaks to
                                 shell history)
  --fabric-password-file <path>  Read the Fabric admin password from a file
                                 (chmod 600)
  --fabric-token <token>         OAuth bearer token (env: FABRIC_TOKEN) —
                                 reserved for future Fabric bearer support
  --target <url>                 Override the Fabric URL template
                                 (https://<cluster>.<org>.harperfabric.com)
  --project <name>               Component name in Fabric (default: "flair")
  --pkg-version <semver>         Override version label (default: installed
                                 package version)
  --no-replicated                Disable cluster-wide replication (default:
                                 replicated=true)
  --no-restart                   Do not restart the component after deploy
                                 (default: restart=true)
  --dry-run                      Resolve package, validate args, skip the deploy
                                 call
  --package-root <dir>           Override package root (mainly for testing)
  --deployment-timeout <ms>      Milliseconds harper waits for cluster-wide peer
                                 replication (env: FABRIC_DEPLOYMENT_TIMEOUT;
                                 default: 600000 — harper's own 120s default is
                                 too short for Fabric)
  --install-timeout <ms>         Milliseconds harper waits for package install
                                 (env: FABRIC_INSTALL_TIMEOUT; default: 600000)
  --no-verify                    Skip post-deploy served-API verification
                                 (default: verify — on by design, so the CLI
                                 can't report success on an empty/broken deploy)
  --verify-timeout <ms>          Milliseconds to wait for the served API to
                                 settle after harper's post-deploy restart
                                 before verifying (default: 300000)
  --verify-resource <name>       Resource to verify is serving after deploy
                                 (repeatable; default: derived from the deployed
                                 package's dist/resources) (default: [])
  --deploy-retries <n>           Retry the full harper deploy this many times,
                                 ONLY when peer replication is positively
                                 observed not to converge (default: 0 — retrying
                                 re-runs harper's component install and can
                                 escalate a transient replication warning into a
                                 hard ENOTEMPTY install failure; see flair#878)
                                 (default: "0")
  --ignore-replication-errors    If peer replication still hasn't converged,
                                 treat it as a non-fatal warning and succeed
                                 with an origin-only deploy (the peer catches up
                                 via federation sync or a later deploy)
  --no-convergence-check         Skip the post-replication-error convergence
                                 poll and fail on harper's error verbatim
                                 (default: poll — Harper replicates
                                 asynchronously, so its error is a snapshot, not
                                 a verdict; flair#878)
  --convergence-timeout <ms>     How long to wait for peer replication to
                                 converge before reporting a replication failure
                                 (default: 180000)
  --no-fleet-verify              Skip the automatic post-deploy fleet
                                 convergence sweep (default: sweep runs — see
                                 flair#636)
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                  output the version number

----- flair fleet -----
Usage: flair fleet [options] [command]

Fabric fleet operations (post-deploy convergence verification)

Options:
  -h, --help        display help for command

Commands:
  verify [options]  Sweep a Fabric origin + its known federation peers for
                    version/health convergence
  help [command]    display help for command

----- flair fleet verify -----
Usage: flair fleet verify [options]

Sweep a Fabric origin + its known federation peers for version/health
convergence

Options:
  --target <url>                 Fabric URL to verify (the origin node)
  --fabric-user <user>           Fabric admin username (env: FABRIC_USER —
                                 preferred; inline leaks to ps/shell history)
  --fabric-password <pass>       Fabric admin password (prefer FABRIC_PASSWORD
                                 env or --fabric-password-file; inline leaks to
                                 shell history)
  --fabric-password-file <path>  Read the Fabric admin password from a mode-0600
                                 file (keeps it out of argv and env)
  --expect-version <semver>      Version every node must report (default: the
                                 origin's own reported version — a
                                 self-consistency check)
  --timeout <ms>                 Per-node /Health poll timeout in ms (default:
                                 "60000")
  --json                         Emit JSON (also: pipe + FLAIR_OUTPUT=json)
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                  output the version number

Exit codes:
  0  all probed nodes verified (unverifiable peers — no endpoint on file —
     are listed as a warning and do not fail the run)
  1  origin failed (unreachable, unauthenticated, or wrong version)
  2  a reachable node diverged (wrong version) — NOT converged
  3  a reachable peer was unreachable or rejected auth (not unverifiable)

"peer" here means a Flair federation peer (GET /FederationPeers on the
origin) — NOT Harper's own cluster-replication nodes, which the OSS
harper build this CLI ships does not expose (cluster_status is
a harper-pro-only operation). A Fabric replica that was never
federation-paired (`flair federation pair`) is invisible to this sweep —
see src/fleet-verify.ts's file header for the full caveat.

----- flair quality -----
Usage: flair quality [options]

Memory-quality report: embedding coverage, staleness, signal density, quiet
agents, recall spot-check (read-only)

Options:
  --port <port>   Harper HTTP port
  --url <url>     Flair base URL (overrides --port)
  --target <url>  Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET; alias for --url)
  --json          Output as JSON
  --agent <id>    Scope per-agent metrics to one agent id (or set
                  FLAIR_AGENT_ID); default = all agents
  --emit          Slice 2: snapshot this report, diff it against the previous
                  quality-snapshot memory, and emit OrgEvents
                  (quality.threshold_crossed / quality.regression) for any
                  crossings/regressions found. Requires an agent identity
                  (--agent or FLAIR_AGENT_ID) — the opt-in write boundary;
                  without this flag `flair quality` remains fully read-only
  -h, --help      display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version   output the version number

----- flair memory -----
Usage: flair memory [options] [command]

Manage agent memories

Options:
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                 output the version number

Commands:
  add [options] [content]       Write a new memory row for an agent (content via
                                positional arg or --content)
  write-task-summary [options]  Capture a structured task summary as a
                                persistent Memory row (used by session-reset
                                harness; standalone-callable by operators)
  search [options] [query]      Semantic search over an agent's memories (query
                                via positional arg or --q)
  basement [options] <id>       Send a memory to the basement (archive it).
                                Removes it from bootstrap + default search;
                                still retrievable via `memory search
                                --include-archived`. GLOBAL and deliberate —
                                scoped to your own memories.
  restore [options] <id>        Restore a basemented (archived) memory. Clears
                                archived/archivedAt/archivedBy. GLOBAL and
                                deliberate — this un-retires the memory for
                                EVERY session, not a session-local view
                                (per-session reuse is drawers, which do not
                                exist yet). Scoped to your own memories.
  list [options]                List an agent's memories (optionally filtered by
                                --tag or embedding-backfill triage)
  hygiene [options]             Detect and (with --apply) remove junk memory
                                rows from the local instance
  help [command]                display help for command

----- flair memory add -----
Usage: flair memory add [options] [content]

Write a new memory row for an agent (content via positional arg or --content)

Options:
  --agent <id>              Agent ID (or set FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
  --admin-pass <pass>       Admin password (or set FLAIR_ADMIN_PASS env, or use
                            --admin-pass-file)
  --admin-pass-file <path>  Read admin password from a file (e.g.,
                            ~/.flair/admin-pass). Preferred over --admin-pass
                            for launchd/cron — keeps the secret out of ps and
                            shell history.
  --admin-user <name>       Admin username for Basic auth (env:
                            FLAIR_ADMIN_USER; default: admin)
  --content <text>          memory content (alias for positional arg)
  --durability <d>          permanent|persistent|standard|ephemeral (default
                            standard). Also decides the default visibility when
                            --visibility is omitted: permanent/persistent ->
                            shared, standard/ephemeral -> private
  --tags <csv>
  --summary <text>          agent-set multi-sentence dense compression (3-tier
                            chain: subject → summary → content)
  --subject <text>          one-line title / entity this memory is about
  --derived-from <csv>      Comma-separated source Memory IDs this memory was
                            distilled/reflected from (sets Memory.derivedFrom;
                            used by the `rem rapid` reflection loop)
  --visibility <value>      Writer-controlled sharing intent (sets
                            Memory.visibility): 'private' (owner-only, never
                            visible to any other agent) or 'shared' (visible to
                            owner + every other agent on this instance — open
                            within the org, not gated by a MemoryGrant). Omit to
                            use the server's durability-keyed default:
                            permanent/persistent -> shared, standard/ephemeral
                            -> private (flair#509)
  --entities <csv>          Comma-separated entity vocabulary strings this
                            record touches (type:value from the closed type set,
                            e.g. repo:tpsdev-ai/flair — see
                            docs/entity-vocabulary.md; feeds `flair attention`)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version             output the version number

----- flair search -----
Usage: flair search [options] <query>

Search memories by meaning (shortcut for memory search) — filterable, with
--explain ranking

Options:
  --agent <id>               Agent ID (or set FLAIR_AGENT_ID env)
  --limit <n>                Max results (default: "5")
  --port <port>              Harper HTTP port
  --url <url>                Flair base URL (overrides --port)
  --target <url>             Remote Flair URL (env: FLAIR_TARGET; alias for
                             --url)
  --key <path>               Ed25519 private key path
  --tag <tag>                Filter to memories carrying this tag
  --subject <subject>        Filter to memories carrying this subject
                             (case-insensitive)
  --subjects <list>          Comma-separated list of subjects to OR-filter
                             (case-insensitive)
  --since <iso-or-relative>  Only memories created after this point (ISO 8601 or
                             '7d'/'24h'/'30m')
  --as-of <iso>              Temporal validity: only memories valid at this
                             point (ISO 8601)
  --include-superseded       Include memories that have been superseded
  --scoring <mode>           Scoring mode: raw (default) uses cosine
                             similarity/BM25 only; composite re-ranks by
                             durability/recency/retrieval (measurably hurts
                             precision as of flair#623 — opt-in only) (default:
                             "raw")
  --min-score <n>            Drop results below this score (0..1) (default: "0")
  --durability <level>       Filter to permanent|persistent|standard|ephemeral
                             (client-side)
  --source <name>            Filter by source/agentId (client-side)
  --explain                  Show score breakdown (raw, composite, durability,
                             age, usage) per hit — also added to --json output
                             as _explain
  --json                     Output raw JSON array
  -h, --help                 display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version              output the version number

----- flair relationship -----
Usage: flair relationship [options] [command]

Manage agent relationship triples (knowledge graph)

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version   output the version number

Commands:
  add [options]   Record that <subject> <predicate> <object> — an explicit
                  entity-to-entity relationship triple. Re-asserting the SAME
                  triple (same subject/predicate/object) UPSERTS the existing
                  row rather than duplicating it. Predicate is free text;
                  recommended vocabulary: manages, works_on, reviews,
                  depends_on, replaces, owns, reports_to, advises. To CONTRADICT
                  a prior relationship: changing the predicate creates a
                  SEPARATE row and does NOT auto-close the old one — re-assert
                  the OLD triple with --valid-to set to now (or delete it)
                  before/after writing the new one.
  help [command]  display help for command

----- flair relationship add -----
Usage: flair relationship add [options]

Record that <subject> <predicate> <object> — an explicit entity-to-entity
relationship triple. Re-asserting the SAME triple (same
subject/predicate/object) UPSERTS the existing row rather than duplicating it.
Predicate is free text; recommended vocabulary: manages, works_on, reviews,
depends_on, replaces, owns, reports_to, advises. To CONTRADICT a prior
relationship: changing the predicate creates a SEPARATE row and does NOT
auto-close the old one — re-assert the OLD triple with --valid-to set to now (or
delete it) before/after writing the new one.

Options:
  --agent <id>
  --subject <text>    Source entity (e.g. 'nathan')
  --predicate <text>  Relationship type, free text (e.g. 'manages')
  --object <text>     Target entity (e.g. 'flair')
  --confidence <n>    0.0-1.0, how certain (default 1.0 = explicitly stated)
  --valid-from <iso>  ISO timestamp this relationship became true (default: now)
  --valid-to <iso>    ISO timestamp this relationship ended (leave unset for an
                      active relationship)
  --source <text>     Where this was learned from (a memory ID, conversation,
                      etc.)
  -h, --help          display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version       output the version number

----- flair bridge -----
Usage: flair bridge [options] [command]

Manage memory bridges (import/export between Flair and foreign systems)

Options:
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Global Options:
  -v, --version                  output the version number

Commands:
  list [options]                 List installed bridges across project YAML,
                                 user YAML, npm packages, and built-ins
  scaffold [options] <name>      Emit starter files for a new bridge. Choose
                                 --file (YAML, declarative) or --api (TS code
                                 plugin)
  import [options] <name> [src]  Import memories from a foreign system into
                                 Flair via a bridge (Shape A YAML / built-in)
  export [options] <name> <dst>  Export memories from Flair to a foreign system
                                 via a bridge (Shape A YAML / built-in)
  test [options] <name>          Round-trip a bridge through its fixture: import
                                 → export → re-import → diff. Pass iff the
                                 stable fields (content/subject/tags/durability)
                                 match.
  allow <name>                   Approve an npm code-plugin bridge for
                                 execution. Approval is pinned to the package's
                                 location and package.json contents — a
                                 malicious package squatting on the same name in
                                 a different node_modules tree will be refused
                                 at load-time.
  revoke <name>                  Revoke approval for an npm code-plugin bridge
                                 (future invocations will require `flair bridge
                                 allow <name>` again)
  allow-list [options]           Show the allow-listed code-plugin bridges
  help [command]                 display help for command
